behaviour: The narrow successor of U9 (FN-u9-rerun-parser-expects-labeled-line). --rerun now reads the ladder runner's real output for the single group it just ran: a new export parseRunnerOutput({ group, output }) accepts the existing labelled `<group>: N passed` form first, and falling back to that, parses Playwright's bare summary lines and attributes them to that group. `passed` adds to passed; `failed`, `flaky` and `did not run` add to failed; `skipped` counts as neither; output with no summary line at all stays 0/0 and can never be coverage. Nothing else in the contract moved - parseReceiptGroups, evaluateExactMain, resolveMilestone, MILESTONE_LADDER, check mode, the head-mismatch refusal, the idle wait and the archive shape are unchanged.

designDecisions.decision: The labelled form keeps precedence over the bare summary.
designDecisions.why: The charter requires the labelled form to stay accepted. Reading it first means an injected runner, or any future runner that prefixes its group, is read exactly as U9 read it - the two existing rerun-branch cases pass byte-unchanged - and the bare-summary branch is reached only when no labelled row names this group.

The charter's recommended reading, adopted. A row that went green only on retry is not 'the staged subset ran clean against this exact commit', which is the only thing E2E-80 accepts. Pinned by 'archives 2/1 and stays MISSING when the summary reports a flake'.

designDecisions.decision: `did not run` counts as FAILED; `skipped` counts as neither.
designDecisions.why: An interrupted run left tests unexecuted, so the group is not proven - fail-closed, matching the module's stated posture. A declared skip is not a failure and must not be able to zero out a real pass. No log in the ledger contains a 'did not run' line, so this decision is made without a captured example and is recorded as such; the failure mode it can produce is a false MISSING, never a false SATISFIED. Both pinned in the runner-output-reader table.

designDecisions.decision: The summary is attributed to the ONE group --rerun just ran, with no further evidence that the numbers belong to it.
designDecisions.why: runGroup spawns the runner once per group with `--group=<name>`, so nothing else can be in that child's output. This is sound only under that one-group-per-invocation property; it is named in risks rather than defended by code, because the loop's runner takes a single --group.

designDecisions.decision: The summary regex requires the line to be nothing but the count, the word, and - for `passed` only - a parenthesised duration.
designDecisions.why: So the parser cannot become greedy while learning the bare form. 'Running 3 tests using 1 worker' is not a summary and is pinned as 0/0; the seven ANSI-coloured web-server lines in the verbatim fixture start with an escape byte and never match.

designDecisions.decision: The captured fixture is built by code point (String.fromCharCode) and interpolated, not written as \u escapes.
designDecisions.why: `npx oxfmt` REWRITES a \u escape back into the literal character, which turned the pin source into a file carrying raw ESC bytes - invisible in a diff and hostile to review. Naming ESC / MICRO / ANGLE keeps the source pure ASCII (`file` reports 'ASCII text') and the emitted bytes identical: both forms hash to a2f0508731b90b7a55bdf08e2bc45d23c3248f04f9f6239bf670f55673930406.

nonClaims: The REAL LADDER RUNNER WAS NOT SPAWNED in this lane, and no Playwright process ran. The charter forbids it here. Every rerun case injects a fake runner that reprints captured bytes; the fix is therefore proven against the recorded spelling of ONE real run, not against a live Playwright. The parent's main proof is the first real exercise of this branch, exactly as it was for U9.

Because the fixture is one captured run's bytes, a future Playwright version that changes its summary wording would pass this pin and still break the real rerun. The pin holds the spelling that exists today; it cannot hold a spelling nobody has captured.

'did not run' counts as failed on judgement, not on evidence: no log in the ledger contains that line, so the decision is untested against a real interrupted run. It is fail-closed, so the failure mode is a false MISSING.
Enforcement is still PROCEDURAL, by the loop (PK-e2e-80-ci-wiring). Nothing runs this contract automatically - there is no workflow job and no hook.

The contract still reads RECEIPTS, not runs. It cannot detect a receipt reporting a run that did not happen; it can only refuse to count one it cannot read, one for the wrong commit, one that failed, or one that passed nothing.

No coverage was created. The contract reads MISSING at this baseline and at every merge commit in the ledger, because no main-proof receipt has ever recorded a passing smoke, fixture-smoke or membership-smoke group (U9 finding F3, unchanged).

The default archive dir is still gitignored (U9 finding F2), so an archive receipt written by --rerun still does not reach main on its own; copying it into the tracked evidence dir remains the loop's job and is not implemented here.

findingsReportedNotFixed.F6: `npx oxfmt` REWRITES a \u escape sequence in a string literal into the literal character it names. A test fixture that deliberately carries control bytes (an ANSI escape, here) therefore cannot be written as \u escapes: running the format gate turns the source into a file with raw ESC bytes, invisible in a diff and hostile to review. The workaround this unit uses is String.fromCharCode plus template interpolation, which the formatter leaves alone. Worth knowing before the next captured-output fixture lands in this repo.
findingsReportedNotFixed.F7: The runner's one-group-per-invocation property is what makes attributing a bare summary to a group sound, and nothing enforces it. scripts/qc/gm-two-player-campaign-core.cjs parseArguments takes a single --group, and runGroup spawns one child per group, so the property holds today; if a future change ever runs two groups in one invocation, the bare-summary branch would credit both counts to one name. Enforcing it would mean changing the core module, which this unit does not own.
findingsReportedNotFixed.F8: U9's F1-F5 all still stand and none are addressed here: SPEC_BY_GROUP is still not exported (F1); the default archive dir is still gitignored (F2); no receipt in the ledger has ever proved smoke, fixture-smoke or membership-smoke on an exact commit (F3); `runtime.playwright` is still not a consistently machine-readable field across the ledger's receipts (F4); the top-level-CLI-pollutes-stdout hazard for scripts/qc modules is unchanged (F5).
findingsReportedNotFixed.F9: The oxlint units config reports '64 rules' for the pin in this lane, where U9's receipt recorded '65 rules' for the same file and config. Both runs report 0 warnings and 0 errors, so nothing is hidden by it, but the two receipts disagree about the rule count and this lane did not investigate which is right.

deviationsFromTheCharter: The charter says to copy the last ten lines into the fake runner 'as literal text'. They are copied byte for byte, but the three non-ASCII code points (ESC, U+00B5, U+203A) are produced by named String.fromCharCode constants and interpolated rather than typed as raw bytes, because oxfmt - a required gate - unescapes \u sequences and would otherwise force raw control bytes into the source. The emitted bytes are identical and proven so: the constant extracted from the shipped pin and the log's own tail both hash to a2f0508731b90b7a55bdf08e2bc45d23c3248f04f9f6239bf670f55673930406, 1083 bytes, 'byte-identical: true'.

The charter names three counting words to parse plus `skipped` and `did not run`, and asks for a decision only on `flaky`. This unit also decides `did not run` (failed) and `skipped` (neither) and pins both, because a parser that recognised the words without deciding what they mean would silently drop them into 'not a summary'. Both decisions are recorded in designDecisions D3 and neither can turn a failing run into coverage.
